agora_applications: Medicine, life sciences and public health

summary.short: Texas SB 815 bars utilization review agents from using automated decision systems to make, wholly or partly, adverse health care determinations, exempting administrative and fraud-detection uses, and expands the content of adverse-determination notices. Applies to plans delivered or renewed from January 1, 2026.
summary.long: SB 815 amends Chapter 4201 of the Texas Insurance Code on utilization review. Section 1 adds definitions of 'algorithm', 'artificial intelligence system' and 'automated decision system'. Section 2 provides that a utilization review agent may not use an automated decision system to make, wholly or partly, an adverse determination; lets the commissioner audit and inspect such use at any time; and exempts use for administrative support or fraud-detection functions. Section 3 expands the required contents of notices of adverse determinations to include principal reasons, the clinical basis, the source and description of screening criteria and review procedures, and the complaint and appeal process, including appeal to an independent review organization. Section 4 applies the amended chapter to utilization review for health benefit plans delivered, issued for delivery, or renewed on or after January 1, 2026; earlier review remains under prior law. Section 5 sets the effective date as September 1, 2025. The text states no penalties.

notes: Text is the enrolled bill (S.B. 815, 2025) with no session-law history or consolidated code text. Section 3 reproduces amended §4201.303(a) in full without marking the changed words, so the change cannot be identified from this text. Section 2(c) excludes administrative support and fraud-detection uses from the §4201.156(a) prohibition. The defined term 'artificial intelligence system' (§4201.002(1-b)) is not used in §4201.156(a), which refers to 'automated decision system'. Section 4 applies the Chapter 4201 amendments to plans delivered, issued for delivery, or renewed on or after January 1, 2026, while Section 5 sets the general effective date as September 1, 2025.

definitions.defined_in: Insurance Code Sec. 4201.002(1) (as amended by Sec. 1)

evidence.quote: "Adverse determination" means a determination by a utilization review agent that health care services provided or proposed to be provided to a patient are not medically necessary or appropriate or are experimental or investigational.
"Algorithm" means a computerized procedure consisting of a set of steps used to accomplish a determined task.
"Artificial intelligence system" means any machine learning-based system that, for any explicit or implicit objective, infers from the inputs the system receives how to generate outputs

"Automated decision system" means an algorithm, including an algorithm incorporating an artificial intelligence system, that uses data-based analytics to make, suggest, or recommend certain determinations, decisions, judgments, or conclusions.

thresholds.note: The text sets no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. Applicability is tied to dates (plans delivered or renewed on or after January 1, 2026, Sec. 4; effective September 1, 2025, Sec. 5), which are recorded as events rather than thresholds.

enforcement.note: The document contains no sanction, fine, penalty, licence revocation or other enforcement provision. Section 2 adds Sec. 4201.156, whose subsection (a) prohibits use of an automated decision system for adverse determinations and whose subsection (b) gives the commissioner audit and inspection power; neither states a sanction. The text does not cross-reference a penalty provision, and the amended Insurance Code's general penalty provisions are not part of this document.
